title: Antihypertensive Classes: Mechanisms and Adverse Effects
subject: Drug of Choice
preview: ACE inhibitors and ARBs reduce renin–angiotensin signaling; dihydropyridine calcium blockers predominantly relax vascular smooth muscle.
quickRevision: ACE inhibitors and ARBs reduce renin–angiotensin signaling; dihydropyridine calcium blockers predominantly relax vascular smooth muscle.
ACE inhibitors may cause cough and angioedema; both ACE inhibitors and ARBs require potassium and kidney-function consideration.
Selection depends on age, pregnancy, kidney disease, coronary disease and other patient characteristics.

sections.title: Essential distinctions
points: ACE inhibitors and ARBs reduce renin–angiotensin signaling; dihydropyridine calcium blockers predominantly relax vascular smooth muscle.
Thiazide-type diuretics, calcium-channel blockers and renin–angiotensin blockers are common first-line classes in appropriate patients.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: ACE inhibitors and ARBs must not be combined routinely because harm can outweigh benefit.

quiz.question: Which adverse effect is characteristic of ACE inhibitors?
quiz.explanation: Dry cough. ACE inhibitors may cause cough and angioedema; both ACE inhibitors and ARBs require potassium and kidney-function consideration.
